svg.title: Separate a mechanism claim from a service decision
svg.desc: Two qualified mechanism pathways show that a hormonal formulation may alter pituitary signals supporting ovulation or change cervical mucus affecting transport. Formulations differ; the diagram does not assign every method every effect or offer treatment advice. A separate information-service comparison asks about social/cultural access and understanding, environmental resources, ethical privacy and informed choice, and economic costs. Pregnancy and STI prevention are different outcomes; suppressing ovulation does not block pathogen transfer. A biological effect alone does not settle a service decision.

text.tspan: Separate a mechanism claim from a service decision
A hormonal effect and an information-service decision require different evidence.
Biological mechanisms depend on the formulation
An information service has additional questions.
Social and cultural: who can access and understand the information?
Environmental: what materials and resources does delivery require?
Ethical: how are privacy and informed choice protected?
Economic: what does each format cost, and who bears that cost?
A pregnancy-prevention percentage is not an STI-prevention percentage.
Hormone effects do not block pathogen transfer; endpoints must be named.
